body:
The production OkHttpClient (ApiProvider.buildApi) uses OkHttp's default TLS
validation — it trusts only certificates chaining to the Android system
trust store — so it cannot connect to a server presenting a self-signed
cert (e.g. the dev server on :8723). This blocks testing the app against a
self-signed dev server from a real device. (Unit tests never caught it:
MockWebServer runs over plain http, and the manual curl checks used -k.)

Add a **developer-only** toggle to skip server certificate validation.

Requirements:
- Persisted setting, default **off** — e.g. `allowSelfSignedCerts` in
  ServerConfig's DataStore, next to serverUrl.
- When on (debug builds only), ApiProvider builds its OkHttpClient with a
  trust-all X509TrustManager + an accept-all HostnameVerifier, so
  self-signed / otherwise-untrusted certs are accepted.
- Release builds must force it off AND hide the UI, at **compile time**, not
  just by hiding a control:
    - Effective value = persisted flag AND debug build. A release build
      ignores the persisted value entirely, so a DataStore carried over from
      a debug install (backup/restore, adb) can't silently enable it.
    - Strongest / recommended: put the trust-all TrustManager and the
      "apply to OkHttpClient.Builder" hook in the **debug source set**
      (app/src/debug/...) with a no-op counterpart in app/src/release/...,
      so the dangerous code is not compiled into the release APK at all.
      Main code calls the hook unconditionally; only the debug variant does
      anything. (If you instead gate on BuildConfig.DEBUG, enable
      buildFeatures { buildConfig = true } — but the source-set split is the
      safer default because the code literally isn't in the release binary.)
- The Settings toggle renders **only in debug builds** (absent in release).
  Label it clearly as dev-only / insecure.
- The login screen still requires https — no change there. This flag is
  about certificate *validation*, not about allowing plain http.

Acceptance criteria:
- Default off: a fresh install does normal validation; connecting to a
  self-signed server fails.
- Debug + flag on: connects to a self-signed server. Test with
  MockWebServer.useHttps(...) + a self-signed HeldCertificate — request
  succeeds with the flag on, fails with SSLHandshakeException with it off.
- Release: the toggle is absent from Settings, and the trust-all code path
  is not present in the release variant (source-set separation makes this
  structural / verifiable, not just runtime-guarded).

relates: T-29 (real device/emulator verification — this flag is effectively
a prerequisite for on-device testing against the self-signed dev server).

Security note: trusting all certs defeats TLS entirely; keeping it strictly
debug-only and compile-time-excluded from release is the whole point.
Review the release-exclusion mechanism carefully before merge.
title: Dev-only flag to skip server TLS cert validation (forced off in release)
